rationale: Both independently rediscover the still-live GT concern (rel_l1_thresh=0.2 hardcoded in the engine defeats the new 0.17 model default) with strong grounding, and both echo the reviewer's closing point that the E2E smoke test never proves a cache hit occurred. X packages findings into a cleaner severity-tiered structure with explicit 'Change:' directives and a dedicated 'verified correct' section that builds trust and improves actionability. Y surfaces one genuinely valuable novel finding (TeaCache/Cache-DiT 'mutually exclusive' claim not actually enforced by quality_policy.py) but buries most recommendations inside dense evidence-quote paragraphs that are harder to act on directly, slightly hurting actionability and readability despite comparable technical depth.
